subject: Logic
title: The St. Petersburg Paradox
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The St. Petersburg Paradox.

hook.text: A game offers infinite expected value. You still wouldn't pay more than $20 to play. Something is off.

buildup.text: In the St. Petersburg game, a coin is flipped until tails. Payoff doubles each round: $2, $4, $8, and so on.

discovery.text: The expected value is infinite—but no sane person pays a fortune to play because the big payoffs almost never hit.

twist.text: Daniel Bernoulli solved this in 1738 by introducing utility—the subjective value of money, not its face value.

climax.text: Your first million dollars transforms your life. Your billionth dollar barely registers. Utility is concave.

punchline.text: Infinite value on paper, finite value in life.

quiz.question: What did the St. Petersburg paradox reveal?
options: Money's subjective value (utility) matters more than face value
